headline: Hibiki, “echo”, is the continuative stem of the verb 響く (hibiku), “to echo”.

sources.quote: The 連(れん)用(よう)形(けい) (ren'yōkei, “stem or continuative form”) of the verb 響(ひび)く (hibiku, “to echo”).

examples.ja: その手紙には強制的なひびきがあるし、さらに悪いことには、思いやりがない。
examples.en: The letter sounds forced, what is worse, insincere.

headline: Chokuzen is Sinitic, built from 直 (choku, “direct, straight”) and 前 (zen, “front, forward; before”); the date of borrowing is unknown.

sources.quote: Sinitic, composed of 直 (choku, “direct, straight”) + 前 (zen, “front, forward; before”). Date of borrowing unknown.

examples.ja: 試合の直前にはいつもあがっています。
examples.en: I always get nervous just before a match.

examples.ja: 舞が家出を敢行する、直前のことだろう。
examples.en: That was probably just before Mai took the drastic step of leaving home.

meaning: to raise, to lift, to boost
headline: Takameru is the root of 高い (takai, “high, tall”) plus -meru, developed from the Classical Japanese verb 高む (takamu).

sources.quote: 高(たか) (taka, root of 高(たか)い (takai, “high, tall”)) + める (-meru, “-ify, -en”), developed from Classical Japanese 高(たか)む (takamu).
Development

Natural progression from Old and Classical Japanese 下(しも)二(に)段(だん)活(かつ)用(よう) (shimo nidan katsuyō, “lower bigrade conjugation”) verbs ending in -u to modern Japanese 下(しも)一(いち)段(だん)活(かつ)用(よう) (shimo ichidan katsuyō, “lower monograde conjugation”) verbs ending in -eru.

examples.ja: その小説は彼の名声を高めた。
examples.en: The novel added to his reputation.

examples.ja: その小説は彼の名声を更に高めた。
examples.en: The novel added to his reputation.

headline: “To embrace” lost its first syllable: idaku shifted to daku.

sources.quote: /idaku/ → /daku/
Shift from idaku.

Compare the shift of 茨(いばら) (ibara, “bramble, briar”) → 薔薇(ばら) (bara, “rose”), or Classical いでる (ideru) and いだす (idasu) to modern 出(で)る (deru, “to come out, to appear”) and 出(だ)す (dasu, “to take out, to put out”).
First cited to the Utsubo Monogatari of roughly 999 CE.

headline: Ayamari, “error”, is the continuative stem of the verb 誤る (ayamaru).

sources.quote: 連(れん)用(よう)形(けい) (ren'yōkei, “stem or continuative form”) of the verb 誤(あやま)る (ayamaru).

examples.ja: 誤りを直せ。
examples.en: Correct errors.

examples.ja: 弘法も筆の誤り。
examples.en: Even the worthy Homer sometimes nods.

pos: nouns which may take the genitive case particle 'no'
headline: Shōmen is ultimately from Middle Chinese 正面, and is first attested in the early 1200s.

sources.quote: Ultimately from Middle Chinese 正面 (MC tsyeng|tsyengH mjienH).
First attested in the early 1200s.

examples.ja: 正面のドアは鍵がかかったままだった。
examples.en: The front door remained locked.

examples.ja: 暖炉の正面にくるようにソファーを動かしなさい。
examples.en: Shift the sofa so that it faces the fireplace.

headline: Yū, “superiority”, is from Middle Chinese 優.

sources.quote: From Middle Chinese 優 (MC 'juw).

headline: Rajikase is a syllabic abbreviation of rajio kasetto, from English “radio cassette recorder”.

sources.quote: Syllabic abbreviation of ラジオカセット (rajio kasetto), from English radio cassette recorder.

pos: noun or participle which takes the aux. verb suru
headline: Kinyū is from Sinitic 記入, which Mandarin reads jìrù.

sources.quote: From Sinitic 記入 /记入 (jìrù).

examples.ja: 事務員は原簿に記入した。
examples.en: The clerk made an entry in his ledger.

examples.ja: 紙に自分の名を記入した。
examples.en: I filled in my name on the paper.

headline: Yameru's etymology note is a single pointer: see 止める (yameru).

sources.quote: See止(や)める (yameru).

examples.ja: 彼は無断でやめた。
examples.en: He quit without notice.

examples.ja: 彼は大臣を辞めた。
examples.en: He resigned from the Cabinet.

pos: noun or participle which takes the aux. verb suru
headline: Keibi joins kei (警, “guard against”) and bi (備, “preparations”).

sources.quote: From kei (警, guard against) + bi (備, preparations).

examples.ja: 警戒は警備。
examples.en: Forewarned is forearmed.

examples.ja: たくさんの警官がホールを警備した。
examples.en: A lot of policemen guarded the hall.

headline: Kawase is an alteration of 交わし (kawashi, “an exchange”), from the verb 交わす (kawasu, “to exchange”).

sources.quote: Alteration of 交(か)わし (kawashi, “an exchange”), from 交(か)わす (kawasu, “to exchange”).

headline: Shinri is 心 (shin, “heart”) plus 理 (ri, “basic principle”).

sources.quote: From 心 (shin, “heart”) + 理 (ri, “basic principle”).
;"psychology"

examples.ja: 私は彼の心理が分からない。
examples.en: I can't understand his psychology.

examples.ja: 彼女は夫の心理を心得ている。
examples.en: She knows her husband's psychology.

headline: Monji is from Middle Chinese 文字, literally “writing + character”.

sources.quote: From Middle Chinese 文字 (MC mjun dziH, literally “writing + character”). Compare modern Cantonese reading man⁴ zi⁶.

pos: nouns which may take the genitive case particle 'no'
headline: Shōsū is 小 (shō, “small, little”) plus 数 (sū, “number”).

sources.quote: From 小(しょう) (shō, “small, little”) + 数(すう) (sū, “number”).

pos: nouns which may take the genitive case particle 'no'
headline: Chūshin comes from a Middle Chinese compound meaning literally “heart in the middle”.

sources.quote: From Middle Chinese compound 中心 (MC trjuwng sim, literally “heart in the middle”). Compare modern Hakka reading chûng-sîm.
From 中 (chū, “center”) + 心 (shin, “core”).

examples.ja: 市役所は市の中心にある。
examples.en: The city hall is in the center of the city.

examples.ja: 市の中心に駅があります。
examples.en: There is a station in the center of the city.

pos: noun or participle which takes the aux. verb suru
headline: Nikkori comes from nikori, “with a bright smile”, whose niko part is onomatopoeic for smiling.

sources.quote: From にこり (nikori, “with a bright smile”). The element にこ (niko) is onomatopoeic for smiling, and also seen in にこにこ (nikoniko, “with a grin, smile”) and にこやか (nikoyaka, “smiling”).

examples.ja: 彼女はにっこり笑った。
examples.en: She smiled.

examples.ja: キムはにっこり笑った。
examples.en: Kim smiled sweetly.

pos: noun or participle which takes the aux. verb suru
headline: Rusuban is 留守 (rusu, “absence”) plus 番 (ban, “watch”).

sources.quote: 留(る)守(す) (rusu, “absence”) + 番(ばん) (ban, “watch”).

examples.ja: 留守番しててね。
examples.en: Would you look after the place while I'm out?

examples.ja: その子は留守番をしなければならないと言って怒っていた。
examples.en: The boy was cross at having to stay at home.

meaning: to shoulder, to carry on shoulder
headline: Katsugu is possibly a shift from katagu, or else a doublet of 被ぐ (katsugu).

sources.quote: Possibly a shift from 担(かた)ぐ (katagu) below. Alternatively, a doublet of 被ぐ (katsugu).

examples.ja: 彼は肩に銃を担いだ。
examples.en: He carried a rifle on his shoulder.

examples.ja: 男は袋を肩に担いだ。
examples.en: The man threw a bag across his shoulder.

headline: Hazu has no settled origin, only several theories, one of them an abbreviation of 手はず (tehazu, “arrangement; plan”).

sources.quote: Unknown. There are several origin theories, including:
* From ハヅレ (hazure, “other; extraordinary”)
* Of obsolete forms ハ, meaning “open; unfold”, and ズ, meaning “unlimited; without end”
* Abbreviation of 手(て)はず (tehazu, “arrangement; plan”)
* Abbreviation of obsolete ハスヱ (hasue, “tip; end”)
* From 羽(は) (ha, “feather”) and 頭(ず) (zu, “tip; head”)

headline: Dore is a shift from いずれ (izure), through idure and idore.

sources.quote: /idure/ → /idore/ → /dore/
Shift from いずれ (izure).
Compare development of 何処 (izuko → doko, “where”).

headline: Pin is listed with three borrowings: Portuguese pinta (“a point, a mark”), English pin and English ping.

sources.quote: Borrowed from Portuguese pinta (“a point, a mark”).
Borrowed from English pin.
Borrowed from English ping.

headline: Suimen is 水 (sui, “water”) plus 面 (men, “surface”), two Sino-Xenic elements.

sources.quote: From 水(すい) (sui, “water”) + 面(めん) (men, “surface”), a compound of two Sino-Xenic elements. Compare modern Mandarin 水面 (shuǐmiàn).

headline: Ikari, “anger”, is the continuative stem of the verb 怒る (ikaru, “to get angry”).

sources.quote: From the 連(れん)用(よう)形(けい) (ren'yōkei, “stem or continuative form”) of the verb 怒(いか)る (ikaru, “to get angry”).

examples.ja: 怒りは敵と思え。
examples.en: Hatred is our enemy.

examples.ja: 彼は怒りを抑えた。
examples.en: He forbore his anger.
